title: The Newborn Commander | Ramayana Ep 12
topic: Vishvamitra tells the birth of Kartikeya: while Rudra does tapas, the gods led by Agni ask Brahma for a commander; Brahma says Uma's curse stands but Agni and the Ganga will bring one; on Kailasa the gods bid Agni entrust Rudra's radiance to the Ganga; her streams blaze and she cannot hold it, so at Agni's word she sets it on Himavat's slope; gold, silver, copper, iron, tin and lead arise and the forest turns golden; the child is born, the six Krittika stars nurture him, the gods name him Kartikeya; six-faced and still tender, he routs the demon hosts and the gods anoint him their commander (Valmiki Ramayana 1.37.1–31; Next card 1.38.2)
edition: vulgate (southern recension), sa.wikisource; verse numbers cross-checked on valmikiramayan.net (Internet Archive copy)

sources.note: while the god did tapas, the gods with Indra, led by Agni (साग्निपुरोगमाः), seeking a commander (सेनापतिमभीप्सन्तः), went to Brahma (pays off the Ep11 card 'The Gods' Commander')
they bowed and said: he who once gave us a commander does supreme tapas with Uma; order what must be done for the good of the worlds, you are our refuge
Brahma, soothing them with sweet words: what the mountain's daughter said, no offspring by your own wives, is true beyond doubt
here is the sky-Ganga (आकाशगङ्गा), in whom Agni will bring forth the gods' foe-taming commander; narrated only as 'Agni and the Ganga would bring one'
the elder mountain daughter will honour that son, to Uma's joy; the gods, content, worshipped Brahma (not narrated)
the gods went to supreme Kailasa, adorned with metals (धातुमण्डितम्), and charged Agni
fulfil this task of the gods, Agni: release the radiance (तेज उत्सृज) into the Ganga, the mountain's daughter

Agni promised and approached the Ganga; she took a divine form; he poured it over her on every side (अभ्यषिञ्चत) and all her streams were filled (सर्वस्रोतांसि पूर्णानि); the गर्भ wording and 1.37.13 are not rendered
then the Ganga said to him, leader of all the gods: O god, I cannot hold your risen radiance (अशक्ता धारणे देव तेजस्तव समुद्धतम्) (verse card)
burning with that fire and deeply pained, she heard Agni: set it down here on Himavat's side (हैमवते पार्श्वे); she released the exceedingly bright one from her streams

what came forth shone like molten gold; reaching the earth it became gold and silver (काञ्चनं… हिरण्यम्), copper and iron from its sharpness, and from its dross tin and lead (त्रपु सीसकम्); on earth it grew into many metals
as soon as it was laid down the whole forest on the mountain turned golden; from then gold is called जातरूप; grass, trees, creepers and shrubs all become gold
the child born there; the gods with Indra and the Maruts engaged the Krittikas to nurture him; they resolved 'he is the son of us all' (narrated as 'nurtured'; feeding not rendered)
all the gods called him Kartikeya, to be famed in the three worlds
radiant like fire (यथानलम्, ज्वलनोपमम्); the gods also named him Skanda (the gloss is not narrated)
he became six-faced (षडाननः); narrated only as 'six-faced', the nursing half of the verse is not rendered
in one day (एकाह्ना), still tender of body (सुकुमारवपुः), the lord conquered the daitya hosts by his own valour; narrated as 'still tender' (review F2), एकाह्ना not narrated
then all the immortals, led by Agni, anointed the radiant one commander of the gods' armies (सुरसेनागणपतिमभ्यषिञ्चन्)
this, Rama, is the Ganga's account told by me, and the birth of Kumara (कुमारसम्भवः), blessed and holy (teaser line)
Kaushika then told of Sagara, king of Ayodhya, righteous, longing for children and childless (प्रजाकामः स चाप्रजः) (Next card only, not narrated)

learnings.how: Applied. The stakes are in the first sentence (the gods' commander was a newborn child, 1.37.23–30), and the turn, the verse card where the Ganga says she cannot hold the radiance (1.37.15), starts at about 17.3 s, just before or at the opening of the 18–25 s window A1 names (en, hi and gu start just before 18 s; te and mr at about 18 s or later), so the stakes turn early. The 55 s two-beat shape is used because sarga 37 carries the gods' plea, Brahma's answer, the radiance entrusted, the Ganga's refusal, the metals, the golden forest, the birth, the Krittikas, the naming and the anointing; the 35 s shape would drop beats the owner listed. This script is about 53.06 s by lint.

Applied. The hook is 2.66 s, under the 3.0 s limit, with the stake in the first sentence, written natively short in each language (hi: देवों का सेनापति एक नवजात बालक था। gu: દેવોનો સેનાપતિ નવજાત બાળક હતો. te: దేవతల సేనాపతి ఓ పసిబిడ్డ.). Frame 0 is the radiant child in the golden reed forest with the gods' orbs before him, which the engine draws at least 70% by frame 0 (O5).

Partly applied. The density of sarga 37 needs the 55 s shape, so the lower half of 35–55 s is not reachable without dropping beats. Every language was cut to the owner's 50–53 s target instead: this script is 53.06 s by lint (hi and gu are planned about 1.5 s under their render, en tracks its estimate, mr renders shorter).

Applied on screen. Scene 10 carries the share prompt 'Which metals did the fire make?' (6 words or fewer) as its title card. It is answered in scene 7 (1.37.18–20): gold, silver, copper, iron, tin and lead. It is a wonder question with a safe answer and does not invite replies about the sensitive verses. It is not spoken, because no language has seconds to spare. The same line is suggested as the pinned comment so shares/reach can be compared with Ep11.
